record.paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
record.context_brief: New operator ideals with nonzero traces.
record.original_question: Find operator ideals, different from the classes already discussed earlier in the paper, that support non-vanishing traces.

evidence.quote: Problem 25. Find operator ideals different from the above that support non￾vanishing traces.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators acting between arbitrary Banach spaces. An operator ideal $\mathcal{A}$ is an assignment, to every pair of Banach spaces $(X,Y)$, of a linear subspace $\mathcal{A}(X,Y)\subseteq \mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ such that:
(i) all finite-rank operators belong to $\mathcal{A}(X,Y)$, and
(ii) if $T\in\mathcal{A}(X,Y)$, $A\in\mathcal{L}(Y_0,X)$, $B\in\mathcal{L}(Y,X_0)$, then $BTA\in\mathcal{A}(Y_0,X_0)$.

A trace on an operator ideal $\mathcal{A}$ is a family of linear functionals $\tau_X:\mathcal{A}(X,X)\to\mathbb{C}$ (one for each Banach space $X$) which is
(a) tracial: $\tau_Y(ST)=\tau_X(TS)$ whenever $T\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$, $S\in\mathcal{A}(Y,X)$ (so that $TS\in\mathcal{A}(X,X)$ and $ST\in\mathcal{A}(Y,Y)$),
(b) normalized on rank-one operators: $\tau_X(x'\otimes x)=\langle x,x'\rangle$ for $x\in X$, $x'\in X^*$.
The trace is called non-vanishing (nonzero) if $\tau_X\not\equiv 0$ for some $X$.

Known examples of operator ideals over the class of all Banach spaces that admit nonzero traces include the ideal of nuclear operators (on spaces with the approximation property, where the nuclear trace is well-defined and nonzero), the ideal of $2$-summing (and more generally absolutely $p$-summing) operators in suitable settings, ideals defined via approximation numbers / entropy numbers / eigenvalue sequences in appropriate Lorentz-type scales, and certain ideals constructed via dyadic decomposition methods on Banach spaces.

Problem. Exhibit an operator ideal $\mathcal{A}$ on the class of all Banach spaces, distinct from the classical examples listed above, that supports a nonzero (continuous) trace. Equivalently, construct new operator ideals over Banach spaces together with a non-vanishing trace functional, or prove that every operator ideal over the class of all Banach spaces admitting a nonzero trace falls within the already-known families.
artifact.category_tag: Traces on operator ideals over Banach spaces
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is part of Pietsch's collection of open problems on traces on operator ideals over Banach spaces. Surveys and follow-up work (e.g., Pietsch's series on traces and related linear forms on sequence ideals, and Oberwolfach reports on s-numbers and operator ideals) describe these as problems Pietsch was unable to solve, and no resolution providing genuinely new ideals with nonzero traces beyond the known families appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Modern Applications of s-numbers and Operator Ideals (Oberwolfach Report)
status_evidence.snippet: Pietsch presented an overview of important problems that have been left open in the area of s-numbers and operator ideals; the second part is devoted to the future of the theory of traces.
status_evidence.claim: The status of constructing new operator ideals over Banach spaces with nonzero traces is collected as an open problem by Pietsch.

status_evidence.title: Traces on Operator Ideals and Related Linear Forms on Sequence Ideals (Part IV)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of the recent theory of traces on ideals, summarizing Pietsch's approach with open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature still treats finding further ideals with nonzero traces as an unresolved direction.
